title: Amaranthus: modeled ₹699/qtl left, Kayamkulam → Anchal
summary: March 2025: reported amaranthus prices at Kayamkulam and Anchal imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 87% of 30 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹699 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 84 same-variety market pairs screened for amaranthus in March 2025; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Anchal report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: March 2025
scenes.caption: Kayamkulam (Kerala) and Anchal (Kerala) both reported amaranthus prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 30 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kayamkulam reported a median ₹2,600 per quintal. Anchal reported a median ₹3,650 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,100/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,100 per quintal, and Anchal was dearer on 97% of days.

scenes.headline: 65 km by road
scenes.caption: 65 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~1 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹14/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹755 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹565 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Anchal report, the rule selects 26 of 30 modeled shipping days. 22 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹699 per quintal (₹512 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Amaranthus route from Kayamkulam to Anchal was positive on 87% of matched days in March 2025. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹69,900, or ₹51,200 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to amaranthus
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹14/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Amaranthus route from Kayamkulam to Anchal was positive on 87% of matched days in March 2025. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹69,900, or ₹51,200 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
